title: Wednesday evening: Thursday is back on, and two questions on sources wait for you
when: Wednesday 11 November 2026, 15:45 UTC (for the 18:00 London stand-up)
headline: Since the midday brief: 28 releases (v0.1.1232 to v0.1.1260). The storm eased: IPMA cut Lisbon's red rain to 15:00 and the orange wind to 18:00, and Thursday is back on in the lead. After your 'yes, don't use them', Vicky's agents stopped every machine read of websummit.com, its app, Luma, Meetup and Eventbrite, and security@ confirms no websummit.com reader is left. Two questions are yours: what happens to data already read from Web Summit's site, and whether the event platforms are read by hand or not at all.

for_you.ask: S39: data machine-read from websummit.com before its terms were known is still published. Keep, re-source or take down?
for_you.detail: security@'s finding (medium, legal). Nothing existing is changed until you say, per Vicky's rule. The terms inventory is with Vicky to send to you privately.

for_you.ask: Luma, Meetup and Eventbrite: read by hand, or not at all?
for_you.detail: Vicky's team stopped machine reads at about 14:30 (their terms and robots.txt). Lisbon Fringe's brief lists them; its lead conductor has the question (work/49).
